root_cause.text: The `fsctl_set_sparse()` function in ksmbd lacked both share-level writable and per-handle access permission checks, allowing clients to modify a file's sparse attribute via FSCTL_SET_SPARSE without proper authorization on read-only shares or without FILE_WRITE_DATA or FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES rights.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that FSCTL_SET_SPARSE "modifies the file's sparse attribute and saves it through xattr without any permission checks", and identifies two missing checks: share-level writable (test_tree_conn_flag) and handle-level access (FILE_WRITE_DATA or FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES). The patch adds exactly these two checks: `if (!test_tree_conn_flag(work->tcon, KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE))` and `if (!(fp->daccess & (FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE | FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE)))`.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement looks up the file descriptor without any share-level writable or per-handle access check, allowing an unauthorized client to proceed with file operations despite lacking proper permissions.

This statement reads the current file attributes without verifying that the client has FILE_WRITE_DATA or FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES rights, directly enabling unauthorized modification of the sparse attribute.
This statement obtains the mount idmap from the opened file without any permission check, allowing unauthorized access to file metadata and subsequent attribute manipulation.

This conditional check on the file pointer is part of the vulnerable path; if the lookup succeeds, the function continues without any permission verification, making the check insufficient to prevent unauthorized access.

This return statement is the only error path from the lookup, but it only triggers when the file is not found, not when permissions are missing; thus the function lacks any permission check even before reaching this point.
